message:
Okf hide manifest (#332)

* okf: move the demo's per-run manifest into a hidden .state/ directory

setup.ts now writes `.state/catalog.yaml`, and push and pull read it from
there. What kcmd sees is unchanged: both still copy the manifest to the root
of the staging tree under its plain name. No command a reader types changes.

`.state/` joins the demo gitignore. The existing `catalog.yaml` line stays,
because the bq and kb demos still write their manifests into their own
directories.

* okf: point the demo README at the manifest's new path

The OKF section told readers to run `cat catalog.yaml`, which no longer
resolves, and described the manifest and cleanup's source by that path.

Okf setup quiet idempotency (#326)

* okf: stop setup.ts printing 409s and discarding real failures

setup.ts created the entry group, the okf aspect type, and the okf-bundle entry type unconditionally, then caught the 409 and updated instead. The result is noise on a successful run and silence on a failed one.

gcloud prints the 409 itself, in red, before the script can react to it. The demo shares the okf aspect type and the okf-bundle entry type across every bundle in a project, and cleanup deliberately leaves both in place, so the second bundle a reader sets up prints two ERROR lines on a run that succeeded.

The catch on the entry group swallowed every other failure along with the 409. A 429 there left the script exiting 0 with catalog.yaml written against an entry group that does not exist. The reader trusts the exit code and moves on with a manifest that points at nothing.

Look each of the three resources up with a describe before deciding what to call. The describe discards its own output and its NOT_FOUND on stderr, so asking the question prints nothing. No create is guarded, so a 429, a permission failure, or any other real error stops the run before the manifest is written.

Verified against a project that already holds the shared types. Two runs with new entry group names print no ERROR line and report both types as updated, and a third run against an existing entry group reuses it. With a 429 injected on the entry group create, the script exits 1 and writes no manifest, where the previous code exited 0 and wrote a manifest naming the missing entry group.

* okf: reword the describe-gate comment in setup.ts as full sentences

okf: harden the demo's defaults, flags, and gcloud calls (#325)

The demo pushed a GA4 sample into a hardcoded okf_ga4 entry group, built
gcloud command lines by string concatenation, and pulled back over the
same directory it pushed from. Each of those is a way to lose work or hit
the wrong project resource.

Default to okf/bundles/acme_retail, the in-repo bundle that exercises the
full v0.2 signal layer. The GA4 sample stays reachable as --bundle catalog.

Parse argv with node:util parseArgs instead of scanning for a flag by
index, so --flag=value works, an unknown or mistyped flag stops the run,
and a missing value is reported rather than silently read as the next
flag. Validate an entry group name against Dataplex's rule before calling
out.

Give --entry-group to setup.ts alone. push, pull, and cleanup read the
entry group back out of the catalog.yaml setup writes, so they cannot be
aimed at an entry group this demo never created, and they stop with a
clear message when that manifest is missing. cleanup names the entry
group and project it is about to delete, since -q skips the prompt.

Pass gcloud an argv array via execFileSync rather than a shell string, so
no value reaches a shell.

Pull writes to ./pulled/, gitignored, instead of over the bundle push
reads from.

okf: make every timestamp an ISO 8601 datetime with an explicit offset (#323)

* okf: make every timestamp an ISO 8601 datetime with an explicit offset

OKF v0.2 mixed two time formats. `generated.at` and `verified[].at` were
datetimes, while `stale_after`, `sources[].last_modified`, and
`usage_window.from`/`to` were bare dates. For `stale_after` that is
ambiguous, not just untidy: `2026-12-31` names a different instant in
every timezone, so the same bundle can be stale in one office and fresh
in another. The v0.3 proposal already files this as an open issue.

The SPEC now states the convention once in the §5 preamble: every
timestamp-valued key is an ISO 8601 datetime with an explicit UTC offset,
and §11 requires consumers to ignore anything else, a date-only value
included. Strict rather than lenient, because a midnight-UTC fallback
would silently reintroduce the disagreement it is meant to remove. The
§9 log date headings are unchanged; they group a day's entries and are
not field values.

The acme_retail bundle moves to the `T00:00:00Z` form, as do the SPEC
examples.

On the Python side this exposed a live bug. PyYAML follows YAML 1.1, so
`safe_load` coerced both forms into date/datetime objects and `safe_dump`
wrote them back as `2026-06-30 14:00:00+00:00`: the reference agent was
already corrupting `generated.at` on any bundle it rewrote, which is
visible in the committed viz.html files. Making `stale_after` a datetime
would also have walked `is_stale` into a `date >= datetime` TypeError.
Dropping the timestamp resolver from the loader keeps every frontmatter
value the string the author wrote, matching the YAML 1.2 core schema the
TypeScript side already uses, and makes the round-trip value-preserving.
`is_stale` then takes a `now: datetime` and rejects any value without a
`T` separator or an offset.

The regenerated stackoverflow viz.html also picks up a tags fix that
predates this change; the committed copy was stale.

Verified end to end against Dataplex: push and pull of acme_retail is
17 files, 17 ok, 0 lossy, and the stored aspect holds `stale_after`,
`last_modified`, and `usage_window` verbatim.

* kcmd: store OKF timestamps as Dataplex datetime, not string

Now that every OKF timestamp is an ISO 8601 datetime with an explicit
offset, the six timestamp fields on the okf aspect (`generated.at`,
`verified[].at`, `stale_after`, `sources[].last_modified`, and both ends
of `usage_window`) use Dataplex's native `datetime` type instead of
`string`.

Two properties made this worth doing, both confirmed against the API
rather than assumed. A `datetime` field stores the authored text
verbatim: `Z`, `+00:00`, `+05:30`, and fractional seconds all come back
byte-exact, so the round-trip stays lossless. And it rejects a value
without an offset, which is exactly the rule SPEC 11 states, so a
date-only `2026-12-31` now fails the push with a precise parse error
instead of being stored as an instant no two consumers agree on. The
spec is enforced by the storage layer rather than by convention.

Dataplex accepts only backwards-compatible template changes, and a
field's type is not one of them, so a project that ran an earlier
version of this demo has to drop the okf aspect type before setup.ts can
recreate it. cleanup.ts already prints that command.

Verified against hormati-bqml / us-central1 from an empty project:
acme_retail is 17 files, 17 ok, 0 lossy; the ga4 bundle in catalog/ is
byte-identical on pull; the live template reports all six fields as
datetime; and a bundle carrying a bare date is rejected at push with no
partial entry left behind.

* okf: drop the duplicated timestamp conformance prose from SPEC 5

The consumer rule and its rationale were stated twice: once in the 5
preamble and once as a conformance bullet in 11. 11 is where the other
consumer MUSTs live, so the preamble now states the format only.

* okf: drop the timestamp conformance bullet from SPEC 11

Section 5 already states the format every timestamp-valued key uses. The
consumer MUST in section 11 and the matching justification in 5.5 restated
it twice more, so both go, along with the code comments that cited the
bullet by number.

is_stale is unchanged: it still ignores a value that carries no explicit
offset, since a date-only 2026-12-31 names a different instant in every
timezone.

okf: publish bundle documents under a custom okf-bundle entry type (#297)

Every entry landed as dataplex-types.global.generic, so nothing in the
catalog distinguished an OKF document from any other markdown. setup.ts now
creates an okf-bundle entry type and catalog.yaml publishes under it.

A document's OKF type is freeform prose rather than a Dataplex type ref, so
the layout could never derive the entry type from it; it stays on the okf
aspect as okf_type and toStaging names the entry type explicitly.

Index files get it too. They carry no frontmatter by SPEC 8, so toStaging
used to pass them through untouched and they fell back to generic, leaving a
bundle's navigation nodes a different kind of thing from the concepts they
link to. They now get a staged type and nothing else. That rules out
requiring the okf aspect on the entry type, since an index has no signal
layer to put there.

The generic entry type is gone from catalog.yaml. The list has to stay
non-empty regardless: it is what keeps the entry group's own root entry,
which belongs to no file, from being pulled down as one.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

okf: carry nested producer-defined keys, and stop leaking .staging (#296)

The `extra` escape hatch only covered top-level frontmatter keys. A
producer-defined subfield inside a modeled record, such as `sources[].license`,
was forwarded to Dataplex verbatim and aborted the push with
ASPECT_SCHEMA_PARSING_FAILURE, so the failure class `extra` was added to close
was still open one level down.

`toStaging` now filters every modeled record against RECORD_KEYS, which until
now was only consulted on the pull side, and diverts whatever it does not name.
Top-level and nested extras share one encoding, a JSON list of [path, value]
pairs, so `fromStaging` restores both by walking the path.

Separately, push.ts and pull.ts removed .staging/ on the line after the kcmd
call, which is skipped when that call throws. A failed push left the tree
behind. Both now clean up in a finally block.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

okf: carry the full v0.2 signal layer through the demo (#292)

* okf: carry the full v0.2 signal layer through the demo

The demo's okf aspect was modeled on a v0.1 bundle, so pushing a v0.2
bundle failed on the first unmodeled key: Dataplex rejected
okf/bundles/acme_retail with "Unknown property: author".

Model the whole v0.2 signal as typed, searchable aspect fields, and carry
producer-defined keys as JSON on an `extra` field, since OKF permits
arbitrary extra keys and no enumerated template can be complete.

Add verify.ts so the translation can be checked without a cloud project,
and --bundle so push/pull/verify can run against a bundle elsewhere in the
repo rather than only the demo's own catalog.

setup.ts now updates an existing aspect type instead of silently skipping
it, so a project left over from an earlier run does not fail later with an
opaque parse error.

Verified: acme_retail and the GA4 catalog both round-trip losslessly
locally and through Dataplex, and a GA4 pull after push still leaves the
tree byte-identical.

* okf: drop verify.ts from the demo

Leave correctness checking to the live push/pull round-trip rather than
shipping a second, cloud-free implementation of the same comparison.

okf: stop demo cleanup from deleting the shared okf aspect type (#288)

The okf aspect type is scoped to the project and location, while the
entry group the demo creates is not, so every OKF bundle in the project
carries its signal layer on the same type. Deleting it during cleanup
stripped that signal from bundles the demo does not own, and the bare
catch meant it happened silently. Delete only the entry group and print
the command to remove the aspect type by hand.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

okf: migrate format and tooling to Open Knowledge Format v0.2 (#227)

* okf: refocus README title and intro on the format

Retitle to "Open Knowledge Format (OKF)" and drop the two intro
paragraphs that described the reference agent so the opening section
is unambiguously about the format itself.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* okf: migrate format, producer, viewer, and bundles to OKF v0.2

Replace timestamp with generated:{by,at}, move provenance from the
# Citations body section into a sources frontmatter family, and make
type the only always-required key. Add trust tiers, status, stale_after,
and the actor convention across the format layer, producer prompts and
write path, viewer, and tests. Regenerate the ga4, stackoverflow, and
crypto_bitcoin sample bundles in v0.2 form.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* okf: update mdcode demo to v0.2 and preserve OKF signal layer

Replace the demo GA4 bundle with the OKF v0.2 content and make push/pull
round-trip the signal layer (resource/type/generated/sources) losslessly.

kcmd's generic Documents Layout only carries title/description/tags + body,
so push.ts/pull.ts translate the signal into a custom typed okf Dataplex
aspect (created by setup.ts from okf-aspect.json) and back, keeping the
on-disk files clean OKF. No library changes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* okf: add acme_retail sample bundle exercising v0.2 features

Fictional retail analytics bundle intended as a blog-post companion for
v0.2. Exercises every v0.2 addition (sources with credibility signals,
generated/verified trust tiers, status lifecycle with a deprecated
example, stale_after tied to annual policy review, Attested Computation
with executor + attester). Structured to match conventions observed in
public OKF bundles (kebab-case markdown filenames, top-level domain
dirs, dharma-style not: field on gross-margin, saschb2b-style # Cited
by on policy references).

* okf: acme_retail index.md conformance per spec §8

Amir feedback + 3-agent review panel: strip frontmatter from every
index.md, replace tables with '* [Title](file) - description.' bullets
matching Amir's ga4 reference pattern, add missing index.md to skills/,
policies/, and attesters/. Bundle-root index reduced to a Subdirectories
listing with no prose sections.

* Update SPEC.md

some wording edits

* Update README.md

* okf: add acme_retail viz.html and fix date serialization

The visualizer crashed on bundles with unquoted YAML date scalars
(generated.at, stale_after, source last_modified), which PyYAML parses
into date/datetime objects that json.dumps rejects. Coerce them at the
serialization boundary with default=str so hand-authored bundles render,
and generate viz.html for the acme_retail sample.

Fix OKF cross-links to use file-relative paths so bundles render on GitHub (#45)

* Emit OKF cross-links as file-relative paths

Previously the enrichment agent emitted every concept cross-link as a
bundle-root-absolute path (`/tables/users.md`). That form breaks when
the bundle is browsed on GitHub, where a leading `/` is interpreted as
repo-root-relative and every link 404s. Fix by switching the emitter,
prompt guidance, and viewer over to file-relative paths, and
regenerating the checked-in bundles.

Code:
- bundle/index.py: write paths relative to the index file's own
  directory (`foo.md`, `subdir/index.md`) instead of `/path`.
- viewer/generator.py: relax the link regex and resolve relative paths
  back to concept ids via the source doc's directory. Keep a back-compat
  branch for legacy `/`-prefixed links so older in-the-wild bundles
  still produce graph edges.
- prompts/enrichment_instruction.md, prompts/web_ingestion_instruction.md:
  rewrite the Cross-linking section to instruct file-relative links and
  show worked examples from a `tables/<slug>.md` viewpoint.

Tests:
- test_index.py asserts the new emitted form.
- test_viewer.py fixtures use relative links and add a dedicated
  test_legacy_absolute_links_still_resolve case to lock in back-compat.

Bundles (no content edits, link form only):
- okf/bundles/{ga4,stackoverflow,crypto_bitcoin}/**/*.md — 40 files,
  152 link rewrites. Verified bit-for-bit equivalence with a fresh
  `regenerate_indexes` run (sole diff is the synth description, which
  depends on the model).
- toolbox/mdcode/demo/okf/catalog/**/*.md — 7 files, same rewrite. This
  catalog/ is a vendored copy of okf/bundles/ga4/ used by the OKF demo;
  it had drifted from the bundle once the bundle was fixed.

mdcode itself needs no change: documents.ts stores the markdown body
verbatim as the `overview` aspect, so link form does not affect what
gets pushed to Dataplex. The fix is purely about how the .md files
render when browsed as files (GitHub, Obsidian, MkDocs, etc.).

* Drop legacy absolute-link back-compat from viewer

The viewer no longer accepts /-prefixed cross-link targets; only
file-relative paths are resolved. Any older in-the-wild bundle that
still emits /foo.md links will just produce no graph edges for those
links, which is acceptable since the same bundle's links would also
404 on GitHub -- fixing the bundle is the right move, not propping it
up in the viewer.

Removes the back-compat branch in _extract_links and drops the
test_legacy_absolute_links_still_resolve case.

Add OKF GA4 demo (#19)

* Make push work for hierarchical entries and bare-markdown layouts

Fix entry ID truncation that broke nested entries like tables/events_,
and let the Documents Layout accept markdown files without explicit
catalogEntry frontmatter (name inferred from path, type defaulted to
generic, required type aspect auto-injected).

* Add OKF GA4 demo

A new demo under toolbox/mdcode/demo/okf/ that creates an empty
'okf_ga4' EntryGroup and uses a GA4 Open Knowledge Format bundle
(17 markdown entries with hierarchical IDs) as the catalog content.
The catalog content is checked in (vs. generated by setup) so
demo/.gitignore is updated to whitelist demo/okf/catalog/.

Workflow:
  bun setup.ts          # creates empty okf_ga4 entry group + catalog.yaml
  ../../dist/kcmd push  # publishes the 17 GA4 markdown entries
  bun cleanup.ts        # tears the entry group down

* Derive document layout entry name from file path only

Previously the entry name could come from either the frontmatter
catalogEntry.name field or the file path, with frontmatter winning
when present. Make the file path the single source of truth:

- init(): always derive name from path (no longer need to read file
  contents to build the index)
- loadEntry(): unconditionally overwrite entry.name with the local
  key derived from the path
- toMarkdown(): strip name from the catalogEntry frontmatter blob so
  it does not round-trip

Update pull_kb scenario assertions since name no longer appears in
the saved markdown (file existence at the expected path is now the
naming assertion).

* Fall back to default entry type when frontmatter type is malformed

parseMarkdown was passing metadata.type through as-is, which let
bare strings like "Reference" (e.g., from OKF bundles where the
type is a logical name rather than a Dataplex type reference)
flow downstream as entry.type. Those then either silently filter
out at the publishing check or throw when toServiceEntry tries to
look them up.

Validate that the declared type is a 3-part dotted reference
(project.location.typename) and fall back to
dataplex-types.global.generic otherwise.
